value:
Tenant screening (BoomScreen) and leasing CRM endpoints of the Boom Partner API, version 2.

**What differs from v1.** Every `/partner/v1/` endpoint is also served under `/partner/v2/` with the same method, parameters, authentication, rate limits and API key scope. Responses are identical to v1 except: `owner` on a property (list, detail, create, update, and the property nested in units, users and property groups) is an object `{name, email, phone}`, or `null` when the property has no owner. In v1 it is the owner's name as a string. With an API key scoped to some properties, the `properties` array of a user or a property group lists only the properties in the key's scope (v1 lists all of them). Requests differ in three ways: Create and Update a property accept `owner` as the same `{name, email, phone}` object (`owner_name` is still accepted but deprecated; `owner` wins when both are sent); on a property synced from a PMS, Update a property refuses a change to `name`, `address`, `market` or the owner while the PMS controls it, with `422` `pms_controlled_fields`, where v1 turns that field's PMS sync off and saves; and Update a unit with `"available_at": null` clears the available date, where v1 ignores the `null`. Webhook payloads are not versioned and keep the v1 shape. See the v2 migration guide on docs.boompay.app.

**Authentication.** `POST /partner/v2/authenticate` with your API key pair returns a JWT; send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Keys are created self-serve under Settings → API. Read-only keys may only call GET endpoints (writes return 403 `forbidden`). Keys scoped to owners or property groups only see matching records.

**Conventions.** Every response carries an `X-Request-Id` header. Errors use one envelope: `{"error": {"message", "status", "code", "request_id"}}`. Lists use one envelope with `page` / `per_page` (max 1000) and a deterministic order. 429 responses carry `Retry-After`. See the Errors, Pagination, Rate limits and Versioning guides on docs.boompay.app.

Public listing endpoints under `/crm/v1/` are not part of Partner API versioning and are listed here unchanged. Rent reporting (BoomReport) endpoints are documented in the companion BoomReport API specification.

value.description: Owner of the property, or `null` when the property has no owner. Properties that only have a legacy owner name return it in `name` with `email` and `phone` set to `null`.

properties.description: Properties in the group. With an API key scoped to some properties, only the properties in the key's scope.

value: Properties assigned to the user. With an API key scoped to some properties, only the properties in the key's scope.

value.description: Owner of the property, in the same shape as `owner` in the response. Send only the parts that change.

value:
Send only the fields that change. `owner` takes the same `{name, email, phone}` object as the response; `owner_name` is still accepted but deprecated, and `owner` is used when both are sent. `property_group`, `pms_id`, `listing_url` and `listing_fraud_monitoring_enabled` are read only and ignored when sent: move a property between groups and turn fraud monitoring on or off in the Portal.

**PMS-controlled fields.** On a property with a `pms_id`, a field is controlled by the PMS when its PMS sync is on (`pms_overrides.<field>` is `true`) and the PMS has sent a value for it. A request that changes such a field is refused as a whole with `422` and code `pms_controlled_fields`; `fields` lists every refused field and nothing in the request is saved. Sending the current value is not a change. To change the field, send `pms_overrides: {"<field>": false}`, in the same request as the new value or before it. Send `true` to give the field back to the PMS; Boom restores the last value the PMS sent.

The rule covers every field, including `name`, `address`, `market` and the owner. In v1 a change to one of those four turns its PMS sync off and saves instead.

On a single-family property, `description`, `amenities` and `pet_policy` are shared with its only unit: changing them here changes the unit too, and the other way round.

Changes fields on one unit; fields left out stay unchanged. A deleted unit, or a unit whose property is deleted, returns `404` and nothing is saved. `unit_type`, `pms_id` and `listing_url` are read only and ignored when sent. `"available_at": null` clears the available date (v1 ignores it).

**PMS-controlled fields.** A unit with a `pms_id` accepts changes to every field the PMS does not control. A field is controlled by the PMS when its PMS sync is on (`pms_overrides.<field>` is `true`) and the PMS has sent a value for it; a field whose sync is on but that the PMS never sent can be changed. `waitlist` and `external_id` always follow the PMS: changing either is always refused, and they have no `pms_overrides` key, so they can't be taken off the PMS. A request that changes a PMS-controlled field is refused as a whole with `422` and code `pms_controlled_fields`; `fields` lists every refused field and nothing in the request is saved. Sending the current value is not a change. To change the field, send `pms_overrides: {"<field>": false}`, in the same request as the new value or before it. Send `true` to give the field back to the PMS; Boom restores the last value the PMS sent.

A partner whose properties come from a PMS but who doesn't use BoomScreen can't update units through the API: the request is refused with `400` `Can't update unit`.
